title: Negative (artefact): in the FCH field chemoton the amphiphile 'decay' -kap(u+1) is a hidden feed. The FCH bath sits below u=-1, so the decay adds amphiphile there, and catalyst-free bodies persist forever (6 bodies at constant mass t=600-1200 with K=0); with the decay clipped at u=-1 they all die by t~600
summary: The claim's no-catalyst control reports 'all amphiphile decays (9 of 3700 left)'. That is a domain total. On seed 5 (world_noK.py, unchanged, run to T=1200) the total u+1 does fall to 0.0, but 6 micelle-sized bodies keep 675 units of amphiphile from t=600 to t=1200, unchanged, while the bath sits at u+1 = -0.0188 (decay_source.png row 1; the claim's own pack_noK/seed0 sheet also shows 4 micelles alive at t=600). The FCH bath equilibrates below u=-1, so the linear term -kap(u+1) is positive there: kap x 0.0188 x ~36000 bath pixels = 6.8 per unit time flows into the bodies, which matches their own decay kap x 675 = 6.75. With the same world and only the decay clipped, -kap max(u+1, 0) (as the docstrings of world_noK.py and world_nogate.py describe but the code does not do), every body is gone by t~595 (row 2). Raising the bath decay kb (meant as a sink for leaked monomers) strengthens the hidden feed: with kb=0.05 on seed 5 the catalyst dies out by t~150 and 7 K-free rods hold ~2070 indefinitely (row 3; mass.txt). Consequences: in this world bodies cannot fully die without catalyst. The starve and local-ablation forks end in micelles that persist (my review 20261025T1459-c17-review-chemoton), and part of what looked like a 'shared product through the bath' there is this source.

finding.operator: linear amphiphile decay -(kap + kb g)(u + 1 - b) with b=0 on an FCH bath that equilibrates below u=-1
finding.control: the same no-catalyst world with the decay clipped at u=-1 (world_noK_clip.py), seed 5, T=1200
finding.result: decay as coded: 6 bodies, 675 amphiphile, constant t=600-1200, bath u+1 -0.0188, domain total 0.0; clipped: 0 bodies from t~595; kb=0.05 with K extinct: 7 bodies, ~2070 constant

limits: One seed per arm (seed 5; kb=0.05 also on seed 6, where K survives). I did not re-run the fed chemoton with the clipped decay, so whether its vesicles still form and persist with an honest sink is open; that is the decisive follow-up for the claim's E. The other FCH worlds were not audited: the micelle chemoton (20261025T1042) already clips its decay; the protocell and gated-micelle worlds should be checked.
